# Review and next steps — 2026-10-26 UTC

## Executive decision

**No newly generated file is approved for submission.** There is no new candidate TIFF in this repository. No experiment, feature canary, holdout, organizer upload or slot selection was performed. The negative result is an implementation and data-readiness finding, not evidence that the HC3 hypothesis is scientifically false. Estimated leaderboard performance is **not estimable**. The official public leaderboard was observed once on 2026-10-26 at approximately 21:37 UTC: first place was **0.4437** (public leaderboard observation, not a submission-page receipt and not attributed to any of our files). It can change; use the [official leaderboard](https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/306/competition-doe-gems/leaderboard/) for the live value.

## Nine-site comparisons

The [machine-readable audit](../evidence/focus-site-audit-20261026.json) opens pinned versions of all nine requested historical files, checks each one's common-grid binary support and compares directional within-3-pixel overlap. The [pinned files and per-file hashes](../registry/focus_sites.json) are research references, **not candidate downloads**. GEMSDOE25 and GEMSDOE30 have identical binary support inside the mirrored footprint despite different file bytes and outside encoding. All nine fail the literal peer-overlap condition against at least one other focus-site raster. Pre-placement source surfaces and all other historical/parallel rasters were not fully available: a passing or failing comparison against these nine alone is not a complete all-registry audit.

Scores supplied in the request are **USER-REPORTED HISTORICAL CLAIMS**, not organizer-confirmed, and the associations to these bytes have not been authenticated. The [GEMSDOE32 current manifest](https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE32/blob/07806249f4ed3efe70b4fbf866183c32392b7853/docs/downloads/submissions_manifest.json) contains `receipt: null` for the named H33 zeros file; its [candidate audit](https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE32/blob/07806249f4ed3efe70b4fbf866183c32392b7853/docs/downloads/gemsdoe32-h33-h33-2-b2-20261004T220000Z-e5eb6e7e-audit.json) also describes an earlier projection as `UNSCORED`. Neither fact proves that no later organizer score exists. It means the **0.2778 attribution is not authenticated here**. Do not resubmit historical files or rename them to imply novelty.

## Why H33 might have helped — and what remains unknown

The reproduced byte-level support comparison establishes that, on the owner-mirrored grid, H33 is exactly the D2.8 support with all points at most two pixels from the mirrored mapped catalogue removed: 44,090 D2.8 dots minus 6,436 leaves 37,654, with zero XOR mismatches. It is **not** an independent detector. The official [DTI definition](https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/306/competition-doe-gems/page/967/) gives each true fault pixel only the strongest nearby, triangular-kernel-weighted prediction while false-positive mass accumulates across predictions. Therefore sparse spacing can reduce redundant false-positive mass, and pruning low-yield dots can improve DTI *if* it saves enough FP without removing useful TP. Without the hidden ground truth and authenticated file-specific receipts, the actual incremental contribution and claimed leaderboard advantage cannot be proven. This is a plausible mechanism, not a projection or a score.

The [organizer's clarification](https://community.drivendata.org/t/scoring-clarification-are-known-usgs-ingenious-faults-masked-when-scoring-and-are-they-in-the-final-round-label-set/11516/4) says the known-fault mask is pixel-exact; new-fault truth can lie within 300 m of known faults. Thus a two-pixel exclusion is not required by the rules, is not a guaranteed improvement, and can discard legitimate corrections. Whether HC3 can outperform any historical result or the live leader is unknown until a compliant paired holdout and subsequently an organizer evaluation. Public mapped-fault recovery is not the same distribution as hidden expert labels; [organizers do not disclose their sources or coverage](https://community.drivendata.org/t/how-were-the-new-test-faults-identified-data-sources-and-fault-types/11527/10).

## Literal registry constraint: a pre-experiment proof

The pinned 13GEMSDOE spacing-five lattice has 206,895 positive dots. On the 5,167,373-cell **owner-mirrored** footprint, 5,160,724 cells are within Euclidean distance three pixels of a lattice dot, leaving 6,649 cells outside. For any N distinct in-footprint candidate dots, at least `max(0, N − 6649)` must overlap the lattice by the stated definition. At the 37,654-dot H33 budget, the lower bound is **82.34%**, exceeding 70% regardless of geology or training. Any N ≥ 22,164 necessarily fails. This is not proof that all lower-budget candidates fail; it shows why ordinary comparable-budget candidates cannot meet the current literal rule. Automatically refusing these is safer than silently exempting the lattice or manufacturing boundary-biased predictions. No HC3 surface or dots were generated, so candidate-specific correlation/overlap and final-byte validation are **not measured**.

Conflicting sibling recommendations were independently checked: GEMSDOE27's H31 is marked submit-ready against a narrower registry, but 99.61% of its dots are within three pixels of the registered lattice; GEMSDOE31's H31-X is promoted in one banner while other banners conflict, and 99.34% of its dots are near the same lattice. Both fail the literal 70% rule here. Exact source refs and SHA-256 values are in [registry/current_site_claims.json](../registry/current_site_claims.json); these are existing files, not new submissions.

## Shared template defects reproduced, not privately forked

The public template is read-only to this GitHub identity (`pull: true`, `push: false`). It is restored at pinned commit [`07806249…`](https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE32/tree/07806249f4ed3efe70b4fbf866183c32392b7853) and used unchanged. Shared defects must be corrected **in the upstream template** before a candidate can be safely evaluated or promoted:

1. [`compare_registry`](https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE32/blob/07806249f4ed3efe70b4fbf866183c32392b7853/src/gems32/release_gate.py) computes preview overlap but only treats it as a duplicate when `stage == 'final'`. A synthetic surface with uncorrelated ranks and 100% preview-dot overlap returns `passed: true`. This violates the requested pre-placement stop. `scripts/check_shared_gate.py` exits non-zero while the bug remains; it was reported to maintainers as [issue #42](https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE32/issues/42).
2. [`submission_writer.py`](https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE32/blob/07806249f4ed3efe70b4fbf866183c32392b7853/scripts/submission_writer.py) advertises mask **or probabilities**, but converts every finite positive value into `True` before writing: arbitrary continuous probabilities are silently binarized. It also replaces invalid inputs rather than rejecting them. Its NaN-outside audit labels an in-footprint check as a whole-portal guarantee. The shared holdout CLI also binarizes probabilities; see [issue #37](https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE32/issues/37) and [issue #41](https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE32/issues/41). Do not use these tools for continuous predictions or assume portal acceptance until repaired.
3. In `evaluate_hide_and_recover`, a zero-truth cell records false positives in its fold but omits them from pooled block totals. Our independent synthetic probe produces fold TP/FP/FN of `1/7/0` but pooled blocks of `1/0/0`; it is **not a real holdout**. `scripts/check_shared_holdout.py` exits non-zero while the bug remains; see existing [issue #41](https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE32/issues/41). This can bias pooled DTI and its bootstrap and must be fixed upstream.

The template also checks label/features shape in preparation but not their CRS and affine transform; this project's wrapper checks all three before delegating. This repository does not shadow or patch the shared evaluator, writer or release gate.

The official format asks for NaN/null outside bounds, while the user's observed portal message refers to values in `[0,1]`. NaNs or out-of-range sentinels **inside** the footprint are definite local failures, but the cause of that particular portal rejection is unknown. An all-finite zero-outside file may avoid a whole-array range check yet conflicts with the written outside-null wording; this repository does not claim that either encoding has been accepted by the portal. Check an actually authenticated official template and organizer guidance before spending a slot.

## Data and reproducibility

- Initial checkout was only `README.md`, not the described train/inference pipeline.
- We restored four SHA-256-pinned owner mirrors, including the 19-band feature raster (418,912,844 bytes), through the pinned upstream `restore_data.py`, and ran its `prepare_data.py` unchanged. The latter reported 58,171 sentinel band-pixels inside the mirrored footprint. The independent wrapper checks hash, CRS, shape and transform before invoking it. See [preparation receipt](../evidence/prepare-data-owner-mirror-20261026.json).
- The mirrored sample's 60,988 positive pixels are exactly the mirrored catalogue; the official page describes a total-absence example. The mirror's checksum proves consistency with the cited owner mirror, **not** that it is the authenticated organizer example. It is used only as a provisional grid/footprint, never as predictions.
- The shared 35-channel `feature_stack.npy` is **not present** in this checkout or the pinned archive. The generated per-band cache is not that stack. Do not invent or privately reconstruct a replacement; locate the shared cached stack, then re-run gates with its source and hash. The current repo does not contain a trained model or a complete inference pipeline, and no GPU test was performed. The organizer reference provides CPU and GPU environments; GPU is an acceleration option, not a verified absolute requirement.
- The sandbox can access GitHub, but direct DrivenData, Dropbox, USGS and GDR binary downloads are blocked; the official data page requires login. The published [GDR 1391 record](https://gdr.openei.org/submissions/1391) describes well/spring and other geothermal data under CC BY 4.0, while [USGS GeoDAWN](https://www.usgs.gov/data/geodawn-airborne-magnetic-and-radiometric-surveys-northwestern-great-basin-nevada-and) is marked CC0. A record being public does not authenticate a derivative mirror, ensure geographic coverage, or verify every field or sub-license.
- Local preparation writes large inputs and cache under ignored `data/`; no large rasters are committed. Restore with `bash scripts/restore_owner_mirrors.sh`, install `requirements.txt`, and run `python scripts/prepare_owner_mirror.py`. This requires `gh`, GitHub access, disk space and the pinned template; it does not authenticate DrivenData assets.
- [DrivenData Terms of Use](https://www.drivendata.org/termsofuse/) prohibit automated access for monitoring/copying. Consequently the site links to the official leaderboard instead of scraping it. GitHub repository-head freshness is a separate, best-effort GitHub API feed, not a live competition score. The [rules PDF](https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/96647.pdf), §3.4, includes a three-per-week parenthetical, but [DrivenData staff clarified](https://community.drivendata.org/t/submission-amount-question/11553/2) that the competition website's limit prevails. Remaining quota is unknown here; follow the user's cap and confirm the live limit before any separate selector decision.

## Prioritized next work

1. Resolve the registry definition centrally without weakening it in an individual lane; decide whether calibration-only blanket rasters legitimately belong in the all-registry rule. Until changed by the owner for all parallel runs, the literal rule applies.
2. Repair the shared preview-overlap gate, zero-truth holdout bookkeeping, and probability/NaN validation behavior upstream; add the reproduction tests there. Never declare an upstream correction that this checkout cannot make.
3. Acquire an organizer-authenticated sample/input hash and the **existing** shared feature cache; audit well chemistry, duplicate sites, missing values and sampling effort. Ensure no `dist_known_fault_px` column or other all-catalogue derivative enters HC3.
4. After the above, execute one frozen HC3 lane: run each feature-alone holdout AUC, whole-component buffered folds with visible-only catalogue features, pooled official DTI and paired spatial CI against the strongest comparable incumbent, then literal registry checks before and after placement. Stop on a duplicate; do not fill edges solely to game the uniqueness rule.
5. Only after saved-byte checks and evidence pass should a separate quota-aware selector approve a file. Preserve one final entry and accompanying code per the official rules.
